Medical education since 1999

SVS Medical College was established in Mahabubnagar in 1999. The Government of India granted its Letter of Permission that year for an annual intake of 100 MBBS students. The degree was initially affiliated to Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences, Vijayawada; the college is now affiliated to Kaloji Narayana Rao University of Health Sciences (KNRUHS), Warangal.

MBBS recognition and intake

Continuation of recognition for 100 MBBS seats was granted in 2013. Permission to increase the annual intake from 100 to 150 seats followed in the academic year 2013–14. The increased intake was recognised by the Central Government in February 2018.

For applications, use the current academic-year permission letters, seat matrix and counselling notices.

The Indian Medical Graduate

The programme develops the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values needed to serve as a physician of first contact. Competency-based learning follows the applicable NMC undergraduate curriculum.

Clinician: Provide preventive, promotive, curative, palliative and holistic care with compassion.

Leader and team member: Collect, analyse and coordinate health activities in primary and secondary healthcare settings.

Communicator: Communicate empathetically and effectively with patients, families, colleagues and communities.

Lifelong learner: Continue self-assessment and the acquisition of clinical knowledge and procedural skills.

Professional: Practise ethically, remain accountable and observe applicable statutory codes of conduct.

Critical thinker and researcher: Use evidence-based medicine and contribute to scientific enquiry.

The undergraduate course

SVS Medical College began MBBS teaching in 1999. Confirm the current seat matrix and counselling information for the year you are applying.

How learning is organised

The course follows competency-based medical education: a foundation course, subject teaching, practical work, clinical postings, electives and assessment. Communication, professional ethics and patient dignity run through the course.

Your first steps

The foundation course introduces orientation, basic first aid and life support, professional development, language and computer skills, community visits and extracurricular activity. The skills laboratory gives students a place to practise with mannequins and task trainers before patient contact.

Community learning

The Family Adoption Programme follows households through repeated field visits. Students learn to understand family health, living conditions and community needs, with training connected to the rural and urban health centres.

Mandatory eligibility & progression rules

Confirm the regulations applicable to your admission batch with the academic office before making examination or progression decisions.

Attendance requirements

Students must maintain at least 75% attendance in theory and 80% in practical or clinical teaching in each subject and phase.

Minimum attendance is 75% in AETCOM, 80% in Family Adoption Programme (FAP) field visits and 75% in electives.

Internal assessment standards

To be eligible for the university examination in a subject, learners must secure at least 50% of the combined theory and practical/clinical internal assessment marks, with a minimum of 40% separately in theory and practical/clinical assessment.

Students who do not meet the internal assessment or attendance requirements are not eligible for the regular university examination. Supplementary examination eligibility requires completion of the prescribed remedial measures and fulfilment of the applicable eligibility criteria.

For attendance shortages, confirm the component-wise remedial threshold with the academic office: the applicable rule may require more than 60%, rather than exactly 60%, in each component. Remedial attendance alone does not guarantee examination eligibility.

Progression and attempt limits

No carryover into Phase II: All Phase I subjects must be passed before entering Phase II.

Phase I: A maximum of four attempts is permitted, and the entire Phase I course must be completed within four years.

Maximum course duration: The MBBS degree, including Compulsory Rotating Medical Internship (CRMI), must be completed within ten years of admission.

Before admission

Check eligibility, counselling instructions, the current seat matrix, fees, the document checklist and any applicable bonds with the college and university. This website does not take an application or payment.
